title: Chicken Yakhni Pulao
tagline: Rice cooked in an aromatic chicken stock (yakhni) — subtle, elegant and comforting.
intro: Yakhni pulao is the refined, gently spiced sibling of biryani. The chicken is first simmered with whole spices to make a fragrant stock (yakhni), which is then strained and used to cook the basmati. The flavour is delicate and savoury rather than fiery — a beloved everyday and celebratory pulao across Pakistan.

items: 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp cumin seeds, 6 black peppercorns, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 bay leaf (tied in muslin)
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min

method: Simmer the chicken with the water, onion, ginger–garlic paste and the muslin spice bag until the meat is tender, about 30 minutes. Strain and reserve the yakhni; keep the chicken. You should have about 1 litre of stock.
In a heavy pot, fry the sliced onions golden in the oil. Set aside a little for garnish.
Add cumin seeds, ginger–garlic paste and green chillies. Add the cooked chicken and fry for a few minutes.
Stir in the yoghurt and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add the drained rice and stir gently for a minute. Pour in the measured yakhni (about 1:1.5 rice to liquid by volume). Adjust salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy, 12–15 minutes.
Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
tips: The stock does the flavouring, so measure liquid carefully for perfect grains.
A spice bag keeps the yakhni clear and easy to strain.
toServe: Lovely with a simple raita and salad.
